global.littlelogistics.no_connected_inve: This barge requires a connected inventory behind it but none was provided. Link additional barges that provide inventory behind this one, such as a Chest Barge.
This train car requires a connected inventory behind it but none was provided. Link additional train car that provide inventory behind this one, such as a Chest Car.
item.littlelogistics.tug_route.descripti: Right click water to create or edit a tug route. Hover node 0 to complete an in-progress route; select a completed segment to insert a waypoint.
item.littlelogistics.conductors_wrench.d: Can be used to rotate vanilla rails and configure Little Logistics blocks.
item.littlelogistics.locomotive_route.de: Right click rails to create an ordered loop. Click a waypoint to remove it. Click a highlighted segment, then a rail, to insert a waypoint. Sneak-right-click to cancel a segment edit.
item.littlelogistics.locomotive_route.ad: Added Route Node X:%s Y:%s Z:%s
item.littlelogistics.locomotive_route.re: Removed Route Node X:%s Y:%s Z:%s
item.littlelogistics.locomotive_route.in: Route in progress — click the first waypoint to compile the loop.
item.littlelogistics.spring.description: Used to link vehicles. Linked vehicles will try to wait if the train is not fully chunkloaded to avoid breaking the chain.
item.littlelogistics.spring.noLoops: Can't link vehicles in a loop

item.littlelogistics.fishing_barge.descr: For best yield, use on long routes in deep and open water
littlelogistics.ponder.train_linking.tex: Use a Vehicle Chain to link two nearby train cars.
Linked cars pull together until the Vehicle Chain is taut.
A train can have one locomotive and any number of cars.
littlelogistics.ponder.train_routing.tex: Use the Conductor's Wrench to adjust junction rails.
Right-click rails with a Locomotive Route to add waypoints in travel order.
A waypoint beyond an Automatic T-Junction Rail determines which path the train follows.
Click the first waypoint again to compile a repeating loop.
Open the locomotive and place the completed route in its route slot.
Start the engine to send the entire vehicle chain around the route.
littlelogistics.ponder.train_docking.tex: Place a Docking Station beside a straight section of track.
Adjacent, equally-facing docks form one station. Include a position for the locomotive and each car you want to service.
The locomotive passes the earlier position and stops at the front, aligning its linked car behind it.
This blue dock matches the blue car, while the red dock matches the locomotive.
Connect automation to the controller face pointing away from the track.
An occupied dock exposes the vehicle's item, fluid, or energy storage.
A matching train travelling through the station docks automatically.
The locomotive claims the front dock while linked cars claim the matching docks behind it.
The attached hopper, pipe, pump, or cable controls whether cargo is loaded or unloaded.
Transfers reset the idle timer. The whole train waits while any occupied dock is still active.
Right-click a controller to configure its timeout, name, statistics, and redstone behavior.
When every dock becomes idle, the train continues its journey.
littlelogistics.ponder.tug_linking.text_: Use a Vehicle Chain to link two nearby barges.
Linked vessels move together until the Vehicle Chain is taut.
A convoy can have one tug followed by any number of barges.
littlelogistics.ponder.tug_routing.text_: Right-click navigable water with a Tug Route to add waypoints in travel order.
The route calculates a navigable water path between each waypoint.
Place waypoints around obstacles to guide the path through open water.
Click the first waypoint again to complete the repeating loop.
Place the completed route in the tug's route slot.
Start the engine to send the entire convoy around the route.
littlelogistics.ponder.tug_docking.text_: Place a Docking Station on the bank beside a straight canal.
Adjacent docks form one station, with a position for the tug and each serviced barge.
The blue dock matches the blue barge, while the red dock matches the tug.
Connect automation to the controller face pointing away from the canal.
A matching convoy travelling through the canal docks automatically.
The tug claims the front dock while its linked barge settles into the dock behind it.
An occupied dock exposes the vessel's item, fluid, or energy storage.
The attached automation controls whether cargo is loaded or unloaded.
Transfers reset the idle timer, and any active dock holds the whole convoy.
Right-click a controller to configure its timeout, name, statistics, and redstone behavior.
When every dock becomes idle, the convoy continues its route.
